requirements_summary:
Core requirements (short):
- End-to-end E2E tail latency guarantees for trading UI (p50/p95/p99)
- Distinct SLOs for streaming first-byte vs full completion for long summaries
- Client-side timing alignment: browser/perf API vs server-side sampling
- VPC + KMS + audit logs, data residency in NA
- Throughput target: sustained 8k requests/minute during market open spikes
- Cost sensitivity: prefer burstable reserved pool with overflow to hosted
measurement_alignment:
Key alignment points captured from workshop:
- Define measurement windows: 10s sliding for production dashboards, 24h for SLA reporting.
- p50/p95/p99 definitions: measure stable server-side request lifecycle starting at server receive timestamp to server final byte emitted.
- Streaming semantics: separate metrics: first_token_latency (time to first stream chunk) and completion_latency (time to final chunk). Streaming p95 applies to first_token_latency for interactive UX; completion p99 matters for long summaries.
- Client-side timing: E2E measured in customer UI will include network & client JS render; we will provide a standardized client SDK hook (sdk_start -> sdk_end) and recommend customers report both server-only and E2E for incident alignment.
- Synthetic vs production: synthetic baseline to validate hardware; production telemetry used to set contractual SLOs after 48h of stable runs.
- Measurement artifacts: histograms with 10ms bins for <200ms ranges, exponential tail buckets for >200ms.
- Error handling: requests that trigger model fallback or retry are excluded from latency SLO but counted in availability SLA.
proposed_slo_targets: streaming (first token): p95 < 150ms end-to-end goal (server-first-token p95 < 80ms)
streaming (completion for long responses): p99 < 800ms (server-side completion)
throughput: sustained 8k req/min with 2x headroom for 10-minute market spikes
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial proposal: reserve 4xA100-80GB-equivalent for baseline production with 2x burstable nodes for market spikes. Rationale: measured synthetic throughput with our model mix (mix of 32/128/1024 token prompts) gives ~22k tokens/s sustained per 4-GPU pool; concurrency target 600 parallel requests with autoscaler thresholds at 70% GPU util. Pricing note: customer prefers monthly commit with burst credits. Expect capacity lead time ~3 weeks for private/VPC clusters.
sla_negotiation_notes: Client pushes for inclusion of network e2e measurement in contractual SLA; Redwood prefers server-only latency for enforceable SLA.
Proposed compromise: server-side latency in SLA + separate published E2E benchmarks and joint monthly ops review; penalties scoped to server-side breaches only.
Availability SLA: 99.9% for dedicated pool; fallback policy requires automatic failover to a secondary pool in same region with documented warm-up.
